close_reason: Fixed: added BitOr impl alongside existing BitOrAssign.
description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1156–1160

Only BitOrAssign is implemented for NcTypeMask:

    impl core::ops::BitOrAssign for NcTypeMask { ... }

BitOr (the non-assignment form, returning a new value) is not.  The code uses |= exclusively, but a bitmask type used in expressions would naturally want |, & and ^ as well.  Without BitOr, expressions like 'let combined = a | b;' do not compile, forcing callers to write 'let mut tmp = a; tmp |= b; tmp'.

The idiomatic pattern for a bitmask newtype in Rust is to implement both BitOr and BitOrAssign (the latter can delegate to the former).  Since BitAnd is used implicitly in contains() (on the inner u32), BitAnd on the newtype should also be considered.

This is not a current bug — all callers happen to use |= — but it is an incomplete API for a type that represents a bit-set.
title: NcTypeMask missing BitOr (only BitOrAssign implemented)
